title: Let a deploy stop the thumbnail renderer

blocks.text: The photo service renders thumbnails for new uploads on a pool of worker threads. On every deploy the service calls `shutdownNow()` on that pool and waits for it, and on a busy afternoon the wait runs out: a worker is in the middle of a batch of two thousand images and finishes every one of them first.
`ThumbnailWorker` already renders correctly. Finish the two `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/ThumbnailWorker.java`:

items: `stopRequested()`: whether the worker has been asked to stop;
the loop in `renderBatch(...)`: a way out between two images.

blocks.text: When you're done, a worker that is asked to stop finishes the image it is rendering and renders nothing more, in this batch or the next, and the code that called `renderAll` can still tell that it was asked. About three lines in total.
The tests run the worker on its own thread and on a real `ExecutorService`.

cases.says: with no stop request, every upload of every batch is rendered, in order
a stop request that arrives during an image ends the batch after that image, not at the end of the batch
the batch that noticed the request leaves it in place, so the batches after it are skipped too
when the worker returns because it was asked to stop, its caller can still see that it was asked
shutdownNow() on the pool stops a worker that is rendering, after the image in progress

origin.section: Interrupting a Thread Sets a Flag, and Running Code Stops Only Where It Looks

concepts: interrupt() only sets a flag; running code stops only at the points where it checks the flag.
Thread.interrupted() clears the flag it reads, so a check that ends inner work can hide the request from the code around it; isInterrupted() only reads.
